en.title: Fewest Leftmost Deletions to Make the Rest Distinct
en.description:
Each operation can only delete the current leftmost element, never one from the middle. Find the minimum number of operations so that all remaining elements are distinct; if they are already distinct, the answer is 0.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n; the second line contains the identifiers. The original text had no numeric bounds; this site uses 1≤n≤200000, 1≤identifier≤10^9.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The answers are 2, 0 and 2. In the first example both 1 and the first 2 must be deleted; you cannot delete only the 2 in the middle.
hints: Add values to a set from right to left; at the first position i whose value has already been seen, everything up to it must be deleted, so the answer is i+1; if there is never a repeat, the answer is 0.
